title: ReviewEvidenceAcceptanceRecordedPayloadV1
description: The payload member of urn:datacompany:research-event-envelope:1 when event_type is 'review.research_object.approved.v1' or 'review.observation.accepted.v1': one accepted piece of evidence, named by its own acceptance identity and by what kind of thing was accepted, carrying nothing else. This document describes the payload ONLY -- the envelope carries the event identity, the aggregate (aggregate_type 'evidence_acceptance', aggregate_id the acceptance, aggregate_version the literal 1), the ordering key, the time, and content_hash = acceptance.subject_content_hash.
$comment: WHY THIS DOCUMENT EXISTS. evidence_review_service/src/application/services/events.py already contains emit_acceptance, aliased as both emit_research_object_approved and emit_observation_accepted, and it writes exactly four keys for either alias. This schema matches that producer, not document 09's line-item list read in isolation from it -- the same discipline urn:datacompany:review-decision-recorded:1 established as the exemplar this document matches structurally. SIX AUTHORING DECISIONS THAT ARE NOT STYLE. (1) ONE document for TWO registered event types, keyed on subject_kind. The producer's _ACCEPTANCE_EVENTS table maps exactly two subject kinds -- 'research_object_version' to 'review.research_object.approved.v1', 'observation_version' to 'review.observation.accepted.v1' -- and a single function, emit_acceptance, is the only writer of either row; the two public names are aliases of that one function, not two implementations. Because there is exactly one emission path, the two event types cannot diverge in shape without that function changing, which is what justifies one schema for both rather than two schemas that happen to agree today. The event catalogue maps both registered event types onto this one URN. subject_kind is therefore not a decorative field -- it is the discriminator a consumer reads to know which of the two registered names this row instantiates. A third subject kind exists in the domain (extraction_dataset_version) and is deliberately absent from _ACCEPTANCE_EVENTS: document 09 section 3.7 names no acceptance event for it, so emit_acceptance returns without writing anything for that kind, and this document has no third branch to describe. (2) NO disposition or decision field, because the event's own existence already carries that fact. emit_acceptance takes a decision argument and its very first line is 'if decision != "accept": return' -- nothing is written for any other decision. A payload member repeating 'decision: accept' would be a second, forgeable spelling of a fact the row's existence already states, and it would normalize a field this producer has never populated with any other value. (3) NO withdrawal event, and the producer's own docstring is the reason, quoted rather than paraphrased: 'A `withdraw` raises nothing. `09-…:§3.7` names `approved` and `accepted` and no withdrawal event, and reusing the acceptance name for its reversal would tell a consumer the opposite of what happened -- the worst available failure for an append-only record nobody can correct afterwards.' A consumer of this schema must therefore never read the ABSENCE of a later row as evidence that an acceptance still holds one way or the other from this channel alone; absence here is meaningful and is not silence to be filled in by inference. (4) NO actor, reviewer or approver field, for the reason document 16 lines 392-394 states and urn:datacompany:review-decision-recorded:1 already applies: that identity 'comes from verified context and attestations, not from mutable domain payload fields'. A consumer needing who accepted something asks the producer under authorization. (5) supersedes_acceptance_id is OPTIONAL and NULLABLE, not merely optional. The producer's `_opt()` helper writes the JSON literal `null` into this key when there is no predecessor rather than omitting the key outright, so every row this producer has ever written carries the key. The schema is intentionally looser than that one producer's habit: it permits the key to be entirely absent as well as null, because a future emission path that omits an unused key outright is still a conforming producer, and narrowing the schema to 'always present' would make that hypothetical producer's correct behaviour a validation failure today for no consumer benefit. Composed with the released oneOf idiom -- a valid uuid or the JSON literal null -- rather than folding null into the uuid primitive itself, which stays a strict format everywhere else it is used. (6) aggregate_version is the literal 1, and this is an envelope fact rather than a payload member, recorded here because it is the reason supersedes_acceptance_id exists at all. The producer's module docstring groups this event among the aggregates 'written exactly once': 'Rows written exactly once -- an import batch, a deduplication run, a resolution, a decision, a conflict, an adjudication, an acceptance -- are their own aggregate instance at version 1. Superseding one of them does not rewrite it; it writes a NEW row with a NEW id, which is a new aggregate and gets its own event. The chain is expressed by the supersedes_* reference in the payload, not by the envelope's version.' A consumer wanting the order of a correction chain therefore reads supersedes_acceptance_id, not aggregate_version -- aggregate_version can never distinguish two acceptances of the same subject from each other, only from a hypothetical multi-version acceptance aggregate that does not exist in this producer. COMPATIBILITY RULE. Per research_contracts/OWNERS.yaml schema_version_policy: adding an optional member is minor and keeps this $id; any change to what a released member MEANS mints urn:datacompany:review-evidence-acceptance-recorded:2, because document 13 section 8.1 ships event versions additively -- the two registered names this document already covers and a future v2 spelling of either are separate registered types, not one type that changed. COMPATIBLE WITH THE ENVELOPE BY CONSTRUCTION. Every property name matches the envelope's payload propertyNames pattern, every scalar composes a released stable-identity primitive, and no member approaches the envelope's 512-character minimal_fact ceiling -- subject_kind is bounded to 128 characters by canonical_type_token, the shortest of the released string primitives used here, so a payload valid against this document is valid against the envelope by construction rather than by separate inspection.

review_id.$comment: The review this acceptance belongs to. NOT a duplicate of the envelope's aggregate_id: for this event the aggregate is the evidence_acceptance, so this is the only place the review is named. Same reasoning as review-decision-recorded's review_id.

acceptance_id.$comment: The acceptance's own identity, equal to the envelope's aggregate_id for this event. Carried in the payload as well so a consumer reading only the payload of a mixed batch never has to reach into the envelope to learn which acceptance a row is about.

subject_kind.$comment: Which of the two registered event types this row instantiates -- see authoring decision (1). One of the producer's two registered subject kinds today: 'research_object_version' (emits review.research_object.approved.v1) or 'observation_version' (emits review.observation.accepted.v1). Not narrowed to an enum here because the producer's own registration table, not this schema, is what the catalogue gate checks against; a third subject kind gaining an event is a catalogue and producer change, not a schema-breaking one.

supersedes_acceptance_id.$comment: The prior acceptance this one corrects, where one exists. Optional and nullable -- see authoring decision (5). Absent, or the JSON literal null, both mean no predecessor; the producer today always writes the key with a null value for a first acceptance, but a consumer must not require the key's presence to conclude that.

sealed.$comment: The composition form. A context embedding this payload references $defs/sealed so unevaluatedProperties closes over the whole composition rather than this document alone, matching urn:datacompany:review-decision-recorded:1.
